title: Mirror code composition before a shared interpreter
hypothesis: For an analytic function family, composing small Mirror codes before one shared executor call preserves sequential composition with lower active compute and a compact complete payload.
logical_multiplicity: ordered source-function pairs, with held-out phase pairings
fixture: Two 8-phase grids. Hold out ordered pairs with (outer_index+inner_index) mod 4 = 0. Exact composition is sin(2*sin(x+inner_phase)+outer_phase); one-call executor uses harmonics 1..5.

development.selection_metric: held-out NRMSE2, actual serialized bytes, arithmetic proxy, isolated CPU latency

success_gate: Held-out Mirror NRMSE2 <=1e-6, active compute below sequential, and complete payload <=0.85x explicit composite codes.
failure_gate: Quality gate miss, no active compute reduction, or payload ratio >0.85.
boundaries: No learned interpreter or natural task capacity claim.
